question: A 3-year-old girl is diagnosed with iron deficiency anaemia (Hb 7.8 g/dL). She weighs 14 kg. What is the correct therapeutic dose of elemental iron?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. 1–2 mg/kg/day is the prophylactic/preventive dose of elemental iron (used in NIPI for at-risk children), not the therapeutic dose for established IDA.

answers.text: 3–6 mg/kg/day in two to three divided doses

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The therapeutic dose of elemental iron for IDA is 3–6 mg/kg/day in 2–3 divided doses. Treatment should continue for 3 months after Hb normalises to replenish iron stores. Note: this is elemental iron — check the salt's elemental iron content (ferrous sulphate is 20% elemental, ferrous fumarate 33%).

answers.text: 10 mg/kg/day as a single daily dose

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. 10 mg/kg/day exceeds the recommended therapeutic dose and risks iron toxicity. The correct therapeutic range is 3–6 mg/kg/day.
Incorrect. Weekly dosing is part of the NIPI supplementation programme for prevention in older children — it is not the therapeutic dose for established IDA in a 3-year-old with symptomatic anaemia.

overallFeedback.feedback: Therapeutic iron for IDA: 3–6 mg/kg/day of elemental iron in 2–3 divided doses. Continue for 3 months after Hb normalises. Prophylactic NIPI dose is lower: 1–2 mg/kg/day or age-band dose.
Correct. The therapeutic dose for IDA is 3–6 mg/kg/day of elemental iron. Distinguish this from the prophylactic NIPI dose (1–2 mg/kg/day or NIPI age-band dose).
